newsitem.title: USA: IMF says concerned about U.S. inflation risk.
newsitem.headline: IMF says concerned about U.S. inflation risk.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund said on Monday that the U.S. economy was performing exceptionally well but warned policymakers to be careful about the danger of rising inflationary pressures.

In its annual review of the U.S. economy, the IMF's Executive Board said: "Directors noted that an immediate policy challenge was to guard against the emergence of inflationary pressures. Directors agreed that the U.S. monetary authorities would need to remain vigilant."

The IMF noted the U.S. economy was running at high capacity utilization levels and cautioned that temporary factors which had helped to keep inflation in check, such as slowly rising labor costs, the strong dollar and weak growth elsewhere, were "likely to diminish in the period ahead".

However, the fund's directors appeared to be split on the need for tighter credit to ward off inflationary dangers. The statement said "several" directors saw no immediate need for the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, while "many other" directors had urged a preemptive, moderate rate increase.
The Fed raised a key interest rate by a quarter percentage point at its March 25 meeting. The Federal Reserve Open Market Committee next meets on August 19 to discuss U.S. rates.
While commending U.S. policy makers for their "skillful management of economic policies", the IMF also expressed some thinly veiled criticisms of the way the economy is handled.
"The persistence of large U.S. current account deficits and growing international indebtedness would be a concern over the medium term," the statement said.

It also urged the U.S. to "exercise its leadership role" by pushing forward trade liberalization in such sensitive sectors as agricultural products and textiles. ((-- Washington newsroom 202 898-8377))
